scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Look up on a clear day and the sky is blue. But space is black, and sunlight is white. So where does the blue come from?

scenes.name: white
scenes.text: Sunlight contains all colours. Each colour is a light wave of a different length.

scenes.name: air
scenes.text: Air is mostly nitrogen and oxygen molecules, far smaller than the light waves passing through.

scenes.name: scatter
scenes.text: These molecules scatter short wavelengths, like blue, much more strongly than long ones, like red.

scenes.name: everywhere
scenes.text: So blue light bounces around the whole sky, and reaches your eyes from every direction.

scenes.name: violet
scenes.text: Violet scatters even more, but sunlight has less of it, and our eyes are more sensitive to blue.

scenes.name: sunset
scenes.text: At sunset, light travels through much more air. Most blue is scattered away, leaving orange and red.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Tiny molecules scatter blue light everywhere. Follow for more on how things really work.
